name: manual_56e02b
claim: When a peer reports a timeout on an authenticated call, read the receiving front end's connection log (status, bytes, duration) before concluding token mismatch or proxy fault; a logged 200 with a long duration means the client gave up. Gate delivery on a fast authenticated route such as /api/peer-inbox, not the aggregate /api/status. Request paths must launch each CLI at most once per hour; only a restart or an explicit authenticated refresh relaunches sooner.

decisions.notes: 2026-11-04: the Mac's authenticated status check timed out; the Windows TLS front-end log showed status=200 after 10.8 s for that request. The cause was the 8-11 s /api/status (serial phases plus per-request CLI --version launches), not the token or the proxy.
